steps.title: Ask a yes-or-no question
steps.explanation: A comparison checks whether something is true. The < sign means less than. A number below zero is negative.
steps.task: Replace ___ with 0 to check whether -2 is negative.
steps.successMessage: Nice, you worked through the steps and got the expected result.

steps.title: Choose what to return
steps.explanation: An if instruction runs its block only when the comparison is true. A block is the instructions inside curly brackets. If x is not negative, the later return keeps x.
steps.task: Fill the comparison so negative inputs become zero.
hints: Ask whether x is below zero.
steps.successMessage: Nice, you worked through the steps and got the expected result.

steps.title: Keep the other numbers
steps.explanation: else runs when the if comparison is false. Zero is not below zero, so keep it as it is. Only one of these two blocks runs for each input.
steps.task: Write the instruction that keeps a nonnegative input.
hints: The other branch returns the input unchanged.
Write return x; in the else block.

steps.title: Make a receipt from a list
steps.explanation: A total adds the numbers in a list. Start at zero and add one number at a time; an empty list stays at zero. let gives a value a name that you can update, and += adds to that value.
steps.task: Add x to n inside the loop to return the total.
hints: The loop visits each number once.
Inside the loop, write n += x; (this means add x to n).

steps.title: Build a strip with choices
steps.explanation: Put your loop and choices together with less help. Your first challenge follows this same rule. Recall the comparison from your first step before moving on.
steps.task: Return the readings with every negative value replaced by 0.
hints: Start with an empty out list, then loop through readings.
Choose out.push(0) for x < 0, or out.push(x) otherwise, then return out.
